references.text: Matthew's version of the Lord's Prayer (Our Father), where Jesus teaches his disciples to pray, 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come.' This is the parallel passage to Luke 11:2.
Jesus gives teaching on prayer in the Sermon on the Mount, which provides the context for Matthew's version of the Lord's Prayer.
God says that he will hallow his great name, which had been profaned among the nations. This is the background for the prayer 'hallowed be your name.'
God says he will show himself great and holy and make himself known to the eyes of many peoples. Related to the prayer that God's name be hallowed.
A prayer that God should reveal himself and make his name known to his opponents. Expresses the same desire for God's name to be hallowed.
'Holy and awesome is his name.' The psalmist confesses that God's name is holy, which underlies the prayer 'hallowed be your name.'
Daniel prophesies that the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed. Background for the prayer 'your kingdom come.'
The Son of Man is given dominion, glory, and a kingdom, and all peoples and nations should serve him. Prophetic background for the prayer for the coming of God's kingdom.
John the Baptist proclaimed: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near!' The expectation of God's kingdom that Jesus takes up in the Lord's Prayer.
Jesus began to preach: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near!' Jesus himself proclaims the coming of the kingdom, which his disciples are asked to pray for.
Context: The disciples ask Jesus to teach them how to pray, just as John taught his disciples. This is the direct occasion for Jesus' teaching in verse 2.
Paul writes that believers have received 'the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, Abba, Father!' Linked to the address 'Father' (Πάτερ) in Jesus' prayer.

'Because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, and he cries out, Abba, Father!' Elaborates on the close relationship with God as Father, expressed in the address of the Lord's Prayer.
'You shall not profane my holy name, for I will be hallowed among the children of Israel.' Old Testament background for the prayer that God's name be hallowed.
'The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever.' The fulfillment of the prayer 'your kingdom come.'
